title: A knight shields the queen
objective: Create a relative pin: line up a bishop, the enemy knight, and the enemy queen.
description: A relative pin ties a piece to a more valuable piece such as a queen. Unlike an absolute pin, the pinned piece can legally move; you must still calculate whether exposing the piece behind it is worthwhile.
explanation: The bishop attacks the knight with the queen behind it. The knight is legally allowed to move, but moving off the line exposes the more valuable queen. This is a relative pin, rather than a king-based absolute pin.
hints: Compare checks, captures, threats, and the stated learning goal.

title: A defender that cannot recapture
objective: Capture the pawn protected geometrically by an absolutely pinned knight.
description: A pinned piece may appear to defend a square while being unable to make the recapture legally. Check the king’s line before counting it as a defender.
explanation: The knight attacks the pawn’s square, but the bishop pins the knight to its king. After your pawn captures, a knight recapture would expose the king to check and is illegal.
